claims.statement: Pro access is owned by the shared main-actor `ProAccessController`, which observes StoreKit transaction updates, refreshes entitlements separately from product metadata, and uses the lifetime and annual product identifiers `com.akinokaede.termind.pro` and `com.akinokaede.termind.pro.annual`.

The local StoreKit fixture defines a family-shareable lifetime non-consumable and a family-shareable yearly auto-renewable subscription with a two-week free introductory offer, localized for English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese.

Only verified StoreKit entitlements grant Pro: a non-revoked lifetime product takes precedence, while annual access is granted for introductory trial, subscribed, and grace-period phases but denied in billing retry, expiry, revocation, and verification failure.

The controller serializes purchase operations, handles deferred purchases through transaction updates, finishes verified transactions after refresh, and treats catalog metadata failure independently so existing verified access is retained.

The complete entitlement-derived gate vocabulary is assistant, terminal file upload, remote MCP, built-in MCP server, Vault sync, and unlimited Metrics; `require` blocks the caller and raises the shared paywall state when entitlement is absent.

Free access retains the ordinary remote-workspace experience and the first three Metrics cards, while protected callers gate assistant execution, terminal drag/drop upload, remote MCP operations, built-in MCP server availability, iCloud synchronization, and Metrics beyond the free limit.

Native platform views own paywall presentation: macOS elects a single main-window sheet owner, while iOS presents `MobileProView` and uses the system subscription-management sheet; both views purchase through the shared controller and expose restore.

`AppReviewController` records review-request attempts rather than ratings or prompt completion, and only arms an invitation after a qualifying active workspace-to-review-page transition; it requires seven elapsed days, three active dates, five foreground workspace minutes, a per-version budget, and a 120-day cooldown.

App localization is centralized in `Frameworks/Resources/Localizable.xcstrings`; every changed English string requires finished `zh-Hans` and `zh-Hant` translations, and the localization check rejects invalid catalogs, missing or unfinished translations, and Chinese spacing violations.

The iOS widget extension contains only a workspace Live Activity; its payload excludes credentials and terminal output, is bounded to six focused-first summaries, and its strict deep links route to the workspace list or a UUID-addressed workspace.

`ScreenshotDemoConfiguration` is DEBUG-only and binds one validated demo scene to one of English, Simplified Chinese, or Traditional Chinese; the screenshot helper builds TFM and launches it with matching application language and locale overrides.

The Astro marketing site is a separate `LandingPage` app whose build runs `astro check && astro build`, and it imports an explicit allowlist of framed assets rather than serving copied sources from the public directory.
While subscription access is granted, `ProAccessController` schedules an entitlement recheck at expiration or within 60 seconds; both app targets additionally refresh StoreKit access on activation.

App entrypoints use live StoreKit access outside test/demo or in-memory setups, then reconcile subscription-dependent sync and built-in MCP on macOS status changes and sync on iOS Pro access or scene-activity changes; mobile sync also requires a foreground active scene.

Both native paywalls derive trial and renewal copy through `ProOfferPresentation` from StoreKit's validated annual product and eligibility, falling back to an annual subscription without a trial if the offer is missing or unavailable; an unavailable plan cannot be purchased.
`AppLanguageTests` verifies Pro offer localization in English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese, and checks that both app string catalogs have finished Chinese translation units.

StoreKit trial integration tests are manually opted in via `TERMIND_STOREKIT_TESTS=1` and use `SKTestSession` to verify trial and restore behavior, lifetime precedence, pending approval, failed verification, missing introductory offers, invalid annual products, and an empty restore.

On iOS, Vault and Vault search open Snippets and Known Hosts with optional initial queries; Known Hosts distinguishes empty library from empty search results, offers add from the toolbar and edit/copy-fingerprint/delete per card, and selects add versus edit editor title based on whether the entry already exists.

On macOS, the Known Hosts empty state offers import or manual add; deletion has singular/plural localized confirmation text and warns that deleting trust means verifying the server key on the next connection, while editor labels distinguish adding and editing.

The mobile Snippets surface separates empty-library from no-search-results states, offers creation of snippets, packages, and nested subpackages, and offers either deleting a package with its snippets or keeping snippets; package-tree count copy and these creation labels have finished Simplified and Traditional Chinese entries in the shared string catalog.

Known-host and snippet card relative timestamps use the SwiftUI environment locale, while host titles, package paths, snippet titles, and script bodies are record content displayed directly instead of localized catalog keys.

Language tests verify explicit-language Pro offer copy, catalog completion for Chinese in Localizable and InfoPlist, Simplified versus Traditional lookup, and assistant token-unit terminology distinct from security-token labels; mobile tests cover known-host add/edit titles and opt-in real-window card captures of Snippets, Known Hosts, and editors in all three app languages.

AppStrings groups semantic LocalizedStringResource definitions in TermindPresentation/Strings for TFM and TFI, including single-platform text; platform-specific wording uses explicit variants and protocol values, identifiers and diagnostic codes stay with their existing owners.

App-facing resource text is resolved at presentation time from the main app bundle using the requested locale, while the SwiftUI key bridge preserves resource metadata and shared formatting composes localized counts/messages without translating user-authored values or caching language-specific strings.

The SwiftSyntax presentation-copy checker scans TFM and TFI for selected UI literals and verifies the shared Strings/AppStrings owner file exists, while ArchitectureBoundaryTests guards the AppStrings owner and dependencies; these static checks complement the Chinese catalog check and runtime localization tests rather than proving all copy is reusable or properly rendered.
